function.name: run_python_code
function.description:
Run python code, the code is a string of python code, and it will be executed in the current working directory.
Always print the relevant information with explicity print() statement for any of the result in interest or any error for you to revise the code.

code.description: the python code, always use explicit print() statement to output the desired variable and also the error that may arise. function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

You are a supervisor agent for final executive report writing, you will plan, manage agents, delegate specific agents to their tasks, and compile their output into draft of relevant informations, and write the final report. 
        What you need to write is sales report for a specific period of time of a shopify store Urban Thread, selling apparels and accessories.

        YOU MUST CALL THE HANDOFF TOOLS ONE BY ONE AS INSTRUCTED BELOW! DO NOT END THE TASK WITH THE TASK ENDING FORMAT IF YOU DO NOT HAVE THE FINAL REPORT COMPILED FROM THE SUB-AGENTS YET!

        The current task will be specified by your caller agent in the very last message of the chat history. DO NOT INFER THE TASK FROM THE CHAT HISTORY, ONLY USE THE LAST MESSAGE.

        For a final annual executive report, it must have all of the item here:
        1. revenue report: total revenue, monthly revenue, trend, quarterly revenue (handoff to revenue analyst agent)
        2. order report: total number of order, number of order trend on each month, average spent per order, average spent per order trend on each month (handoff to order analyst agent)
        3. product performance: top/bottom overall product, top/bottom product per month, top/bottom revenue contributor product, top/bottom revenue contributor product per month (handoff to product performance analyst agent)
        4. strategic analyses: current report compared to annual strategy plan, target metrics vs actual realization metrics, met and unmet sales goal.
        
        To finish the final report, do this one by one

        1. First you must make plan on what to do. Summarize the request from the chat history. Write the period of final executive report requested.
        
        2. Retrieve the data you need using the tool get_order_data_for_period for the valid requested period, output the file name so that future agent know what the file name is.
        
        3. Only after retrieve the data in previous step, you will then delegate the revenue analysis to the revenue analyst agent by following this step: 
            - Generate the task to do WITHOUT calling the revenue analyst agent, and provide the relevant file name for the requested period.
            - Delegate the task by calling the handoff tool for revenue analyst agent
        
        4. Only after revenue analyst agent give you its analysis, you will then delegate the order analysis to the order analyst agent by following this step: 
            - Generate the task to do WITHOUT calling the order analyst agent, and provide the relevant file name for the requested period.
            - Delegate the task by calling the handoff tool for order analyst agent

        5. Only after order analyst agent give you its analysis, you will then delegate the product performance analysis to the product performance analyst agent by following this step: 
            - Generate the task to do WITHOUT calling the product performance analyst agent, and provide the relevant file name for the requested period.
            - Delegate the task by calling the handoff tool for product performance analyst agent

        6. Only after product analyst agent give you its analysis, you will then delegate the strategic analysis to the strategic analyst agent by following this step: 
            - Generate the task to do WITHOUT calling the strategic analyst agent, and provide the relevant file name for the requested period.
            - Delegate the task by calling the handoff tool for strategic analyst agent

        7. Finally you must review the output from worker agents and present it to the Main Agent.

        You must present the final report in a markdown format without any quotes or anything, ready to be rendered.

        If you have done writing the final report and want to pass it to the main agent, write the report in markdown format, ready to be rendered, and start and end with this task ending format:

        start with:
        THIS IS THE FINAL REPORT DRAFT FROM Final Report Agent, PLEASE PRESENT IT TO THE USER, The user won't see this message directly

        end it with:
        THIS IS THE END OF THE SALES REPORT
        to indicate that the writing is finished

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

    'quarterly_revenue': quarterly_revenue,
    'monthly_trend': monthly_list,
    'quarterly_trend': quarterly_trend

Quarterly trend: just one quarter. But maybe trend across months: we can compute month-over-month change. Also quarterly trend: maybe month-to-month percent change. We'll produce JSON with keys: total_revenue, monthly_revenue (list of dict month, revenue), quarterly_revenue (list of dict quarter, revenue), monthly_trend (list of dict month, revenue, percent_change_from_prev_month), quarterly_trend (list of dict quarter, revenue, percent_change_from_prev_quarter). import json, os, datetime
from pathlib import Path

# Load data
file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Ensure data is a list
if not isinstance(data, list):
    print('Data is not a list, first two entries:')
    print(data[:2])
    raise ValueError('Unexpected data format')

# Prepare structures
monthly_revenue = {}
for order in data:
    node = order.get('node', {})
    amount_str = node.get('totalPriceSet', {}).get('shopMoney', {}).get('amount')
    if amount_str is None:
        continue
    try:
        amount = float(amount_str)
    except Exception as e:
        print('Error converting amount:', amount_str, e)
        continue
    processed_at = node.get('processedAt')
    if not processed_at:
        continue
    # Parse date
    try:
        dt = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.rstrip('Z'))
    except Exception as e:
        print('Date parse error:', processed_at, e)
        continue
    month_key = dt.strftime('%Y-%m')
    monthly_revenue[month_key] = monthly_revenue.get(month_key, 0.0) + amount

# Sort months
sorted_months = sorted(monthly_revenue.keys())
# Compute total revenue
total_revenue = sum(monthly_revenue.values())

# Prepare monthly list
monthly_list = []
prev_rev = None
for month in sorted_months:
    rev = monthly_revenue[month]
    pct_change = None
    if prev_rev is not None:
        pct_change = ((rev - prev_rev) / prev_rev) * 100 if prev_rev != 0 else None
    monthly_list.append({'month': month, 'revenue': rev, 'pct_change_from_prev_month': pct_change})
    prev_rev = rev

# Quarterly revenue (only one quarter)
quarterly_revenue = [{'quarter': 'Q1 2024', 'revenue': total_revenue}]
# Quarterly trend (only one quarter, no previous)
quarterly_trend = [{'quarter': 'Q1 2024', 'revenue': total_revenue, 'pct_change_from_prev_quarter': None}]

# Output JSON
output = {
    'total_revenue': total_revenue,
    'monthly_revenue': monthly_list,
    'quarterly_revenue': quarterly_revenue,
    'monthly_trend': monthly_list,
    'quarterly_trend': quarterly_trend
}
print(json.dumps(output, indent=2))

import json, os, datetime
from pathlib import Path

# Load data
file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Ensure data is a list
if not isinstance(data, list):
    print('Data is not a list, first two entries:')
    print(data[:2])
    raise ValueError('Unexpected data format')

# Prepare structures
monthly_revenue = {}
for order in data:
    node = order.get('node', {})
    amount_str = node.get('totalPriceSet', {}).get('shopMoney', {}).get('amount')
    if amount_str is None:
        continue
    try:
        amount = float(amount_str)
    except Exception as e:
        print('Error converting amount:', amount_str, e)
        continue
    processed_at = node.get('processedAt')
    if not processed_at:
        continue
    # Parse date
    try:
        dt = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.rstrip('Z'))
    except Exception as e:
        print('Date parse error:', processed_at, e)
        continue
    month_key = dt.strftime('%Y-%m')
    monthly_revenue[month_key] = monthly_revenue.get(month_key, 0.0) + amount

# Sort months
sorted_months = sorted(monthly_revenue.keys())
# Compute total revenue
total_revenue = sum(monthly_revenue.values())

# Prepare monthly list
monthly_list = []
prev_rev = None
for month in sorted_months:
    rev = monthly_revenue[month]
    pct_change = None
    if prev_rev is not None:
        pct_change = ((rev - prev_rev) / prev_rev) * 100 if prev_rev != 0 else None
    monthly_list.append({'month': month, 'revenue': rev, 'pct_change_from_prev_month': pct_change})
    prev_rev = rev

# Quarterly revenue (only one quarter)

# Quarterly trend (only one quarter, no previous)
quarterly_trend = [{'quarter': 'Q1 2024', 'revenue': total_revenue, 'pct_change_from_prev_quarter': None}]

# Output JSON
output = {
    'total_revenue': total_revenue,
    'monthly_revenue': monthly_list,
    'quarterly_revenue': quarterly_revenue,
    'monthly_trend': monthly_list,
    'quarterly_trend': quarterly_trend
}
print(json.dumps(output, indent=2))

import json, os, pandas as pd
# Load data
file_path = './runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json'
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)
# data is a list of orders
orders = data
# Extract processedAt and totalPrice
records = []
for order in orders:
    try:
        processed_at = order['node']['processedAt']
        amount = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
        records.append({'processedAt': processed_at, 'amount': amount})
    except Exception as e:
        print('Error parsing order:', e)
        continue
# Create DataFrame
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

if not records:
    print('No records parsed.')
    exit()

df = pd.DataFrame(records)
# Convert processedAt to datetime
df['processedAt'] = pd.to_datetime(df['processedAt'])
# Add month column
df['month'] = df['processedAt'].dt.to_period('M')
# Total number of orders
total_orders = len(df)
# Monthly order counts
monthly_counts = df.groupby('month').size().reset_index(name='order_count')
# Average spent per order overall
avg_spent_overall = df['amount'].mean()
# Monthly average spent
monthly_avg = df.groupby('month')['amount'].mean().reset_index(name='avg_spent')
# Print results
print('Total number of orders overall:', total_orders)
print('Number of orders trend each month:')
print(monthly_counts.to_string(index=False))
print('Average spent per order overall: {:.2f}'.format(avg_spent_overall))
print('Average spent per order trend each month:')
print(monthly_avg.to_string(index=False))

import json, os, pandas as pd
# Load data
file_path = './runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json'
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)
# data is a list of orders
orders = data
# Extract processedAt and totalPrice
records = []
for order in orders:
    try:
        processed_at = order['node']['processedAt']
        amount = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
        records.append({'processedAt': processed_at, 'amount': amount})
    except Exception as e:
        print('Error parsing order:', e)
        continue
# Create DataFrame
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

if not records:
    print('No records parsed.')
    exit()

df = pd.DataFrame(records)
# Convert processedAt to datetime
df['processedAt'] = pd.to_datetime(df['processedAt'])
# Add month column
df['month'] = df['processedAt'].dt.to_period('M')
# Total number of orders
total_orders = len(df)
# Monthly order counts
monthly_counts = df.groupby('month').size().reset_index(name='order_count')
# Average spent per order overall
avg_spent_overall = df['amount'].mean()
# Monthly average spent
monthly_avg = df.groupby('month')['amount'].mean().reset_index(name='avg_spent')
# Print results
print('Total number of orders overall:', total_orders)
print('Number of orders trend each month:')
print(monthly_counts.to_string(index=False))
print('Average spent per order overall: {:.2f}'.format(avg_spent_overall))
print('Average spent per order trend each month:')
print(monthly_avg.to_string(index=False))

import json, os, pandas as pd
# Load data
file_path = './runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json'
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)
# data is a list of orders
orders = data
# Extract processedAt and totalPrice
records = []
for order in orders:
    try:
        processed_at = order['node']['processedAt']
        amount = float(order['node']['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
        records.append({'processedAt': processed_at, 'amount': amount})
    except Exception as e:
        print('Error parsing order:', e)
        continue
# Create DataFrame
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

if not records:
    print('No records parsed.')
    exit()

df = pd.DataFrame(records)
# Convert processedAt to datetime

# Add month column
df['month'] = df['processedAt'].dt.to_period('M')
# Total number of orders
total_orders = len(df)
# Monthly order counts
monthly_counts = df.groupby('month').size().reset_index(name='order_count')
# Average spent per order overall
avg_spent_overall = df['amount'].mean()
# Monthly average spent
monthly_avg = df.groupby('month')['amount'].mean().reset_index(name='avg_spent')
# Print results
print('Total number of orders overall:', total_orders)
print('Number of orders trend each month:')
print(monthly_counts.to_string(index=False))
print('Average spent per order overall: {:.2f}'.format(avg_spent_overall))
print('Average spent per order trend each month:')
print(monthly_avg.to_string(index=False))

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:

        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:
    print(title, rev)
print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:
    print(title, rev)

for month, rev_dict in product_month_rev.items():
    sorted_month = sorted(rev_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Month {month} top 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:
    print(title, rev)
print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:
    print(title, rev)

# Top/bottom per month
for month, rev_dict in product_month_rev.items():
    sorted_month = sorted(rev_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Month {month} top 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:
    print(title, rev)
print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:
    print(title, rev)

# Top/bottom per month
for month, rev_dict in product_month_rev.items():
    sorted_month = sorted(rev_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Month {month} top 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:
    print(title, rev)
print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:
    print(title, rev)

    sorted_month = sorted(rev_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Month {month} top 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:
    print(title, rev)
print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:
    print(title, rev)

# Top/bottom per month
for month, rev_dict in product_month_rev.items():
    sorted_month = sorted(rev_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Month {month} top 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:

print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:

    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:
    print(title, rev)
print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:
    print(title, rev)

# Top/bottom per month
for month, rev_dict in product_month_rev.items():
    sorted_month = sorted(rev_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Month {month} top 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:
    print(title, rev)
print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:
    print(title, rev)

# Top/bottom per month
for month, rev_dict in product_month_rev.items():
    sorted_month = sorted(rev_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Month {month} top 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)

    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:
    print(title, rev)
print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:
    print(title, rev)

# Top/bottom per month
for month, rev_dict in product_month_rev.items():
    sorted_month = sorted(rev_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Month {month} top 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:
        continue
    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom
sorted_products = sorted(product_rev.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print('Top 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[:3]:
    print(title, rev)
print('Bottom 3 overall products:')
for title, rev in sorted_products[-3:]:
    print(title, rev)

# Top/bottom per month
for month, rev_dict in product_month_rev.items():
    sorted_month = sorted(rev_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"Month {month} top 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[:3]:
        print('  ', title, rev)
    print(f"Month {month} bottom 3:")
    for title, rev in sorted_month[-3:]:
        print('  ', title, rev)

import json, os

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

file_path = Path('./runtime_data/2024-01-01_to_2024-03-31_order.json')
with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
    orders = json.load(f)

product_rev = defaultdict(float)
product_month_rev = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

for order in orders:
    node = order['node']
    order_total = float(node['totalPriceSet']['shopMoney']['amount'])
    processed_at = node['processedAt']
    month = datetime.fromisoformat(processed_at.replace('Z', '+00:00')).strftime('%Y-%m')
    line_items = node['lineItems']['edges']
    total_qty = sum(li['node']['quantity'] for li in line_items)
    if total_qty == 0:

    for li in line_items:
        qty = li['node']['quantity']
        title = li['node']['title']
        # allocate revenue proportionally
        rev = order_total * (qty / total_qty)
        product_rev[title] += rev
        product_month_rev[month][title] += rev

# Overall top/bottom

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

## 2024 Annual Sales Strategy Plan  
**Theme:** “Threaded for All Seasons”  
**Prepared:** January 2024

---

## Executive Summary

Urban Thread enters 2024 with strong momentum, closing 2023 at **£62,300** in revenue and **1,010 total orders**. Our focus for 2024 is to transition from a strong core offering into a more diversified, seasonally balanced product range, elevating our average order value and brand relevance throughout the year. We are setting clear growth and brand-building objectives to ensure that Urban Thread remains not only consistent in performance but also adaptable in fashion cycles.

---

## Strategic Goals

---

## Risk Considerations

- **Q1 performance** historically underwhelms; we will mitigate with timely product launches and flash promotions.
- **Inventory risk** on new categories (socks, bags) will be limited through low initial production runs and bundled sell-through plans.
- **Over-indexing on a few high-performing products** remains a risk; we’ll counterbalance this with intentional feature placement for new items and cross-category pairing in marketing.

---

## Closing Thought

2024 is not just a growth year — it is a **brand definition year**.  
"Threaded for All Seasons" is more than a campaign line; it’s a product strategy, a calendar playbook, and a cultural signal. Urban Thread’s role in the wardrobe is evolving. This plan ensures we’re not only growing, but growing with purpose.

# Urban Thread  
## 2024 Annual Sales Strategy Plan  
**Theme:** “Threaded for All Seasons”  
**Prepared:** January 2024

---

## Executive Summary

Urban Thread enters 2024 with strong momentum, closing 2023 at **£62,300** in revenue and **1,010 total orders**. Our focus for 2024 is to transition from a strong core offering into a more diversified, seasonally balanced product range, elevating our average order value and brand relevance throughout the year. We are setting clear growth and brand-building objectives to ensure that Urban Thread remains not only consistent in performance but also adaptable in fashion cycles.

---

## Strategic Goals
retrieved doc 2:

## Strategic Goals

- **Increase annual revenue by 25%** to reach at least **£78,000** by year-end.
- **Grow total orders by 18.8%** to reach **1,200**, driven by new customer acquisition and improved repeat purchase behavior.
- **Raise average spend per order to £69.00** by encouraging bundled purchases and promoting higher-ticket items.
- **Decrease dependency on top 5 SKUs**, targeting no more than **55% of revenue concentration** from them.
- **Expand the role of winter accessories and layering pieces** to achieve at least **10% of Q4 revenue** from these items.
- **Ensure at least 30% of total annual revenue** is contributed by new products introduced in 2024.

---

## Target Market
retrieved doc 3:
---

## Risk Considerations

- **Q1 performance** historically underwhelms; we will mitigate with timely product launches and flash promotions.
- **Inventory risk** on new categories (socks, bags) will be limited through low initial production runs and bundled sell-through plans.
- **Over-indexing on a few high-performing products** remains a risk; we’ll counterbalance this with intentional feature placement for new items and cross-category pairing in marketing.

---

## Closing Thought

2024 is not just a growth year — it is a **brand definition year**.  
"Threaded for All Seasons" is more than a campaign line; it’s a product strategy, a calendar playbook, and a cultural signal. Urban Thread’s role in the wardrobe is evolving. This plan ensures we’re not only growing, but growing with purpose.

---

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

- **Increase annual revenue by 25%** to reach at least **£78,000** by year-end.

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).

function.name: tavily_search
function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.

function.description: A search engine optimized for comprehensive, accurate, and trusted results. Useful for when you need to answer questions about current events. It not only retrieves URLs and snippets, but offers advanced search depths, domain management, time range filters, and image search, this tool delivers real-time, accurate, and citation-backed results.Input should be a search query.

include_domains.description:
A list of domains to restrict search results to.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests information from specific websites (e.g., "Find climate data from nasa.gov")
        2. The user mentions an organization or company without specifying the domain (e.g., "Find information about iPhones from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains (e.g., ["nasa.gov"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will ONLY come from the specified domains - no other sources will be included.
        Default is None (no domain restriction).

exclude_domains.description:
A list of domains to exclude from search results.

        Use this parameter when:
        1. The user explicitly requests to avoid certain websites (e.g., "Find information about climate change but not from twitter.com")
        2. The user mentions not wanting results from specific organizations without naming the domain (e.g., "Find phone reviews but nothing from Apple")

        In both cases, you should determine the appropriate domains to exclude (e.g., ["twitter.com"] or ["apple.com"]) and set this parameter.

        Results will filter out all content from the specified domains.
        Default is None (no domain exclusion).

search_depth.description:
Controls search thoroughness and result comprehensiveness.
    
        Use "basic" for simple queries requiring quick, straightforward answers.
        
        Use "advanced" (default) for complex queries, specialized topics, 
        rare information, or when in-depth analysis is needed.

include_images.description:
Determines if the search returns relevant images along with text results.
   
        Set to True when the user explicitly requests visuals or when images would 
        significantly enhance understanding (e.g., "Show me what black holes look like," 
        "Find pictures of Renaissance art").
        
        Leave as False (default) for most informational queries where text is sufficient.

time_range.description:
Limits results to content published within a specific timeframe.
        
        ONLY set this when the user explicitly mentions a time period 
        (e.g., "latest AI news," "articles from last week").
        
        For less popular or niche topics, use broader time ranges 
        ("month" or "year") to ensure sufficient relevant results.
   
        Options: "day" (24h), "week" (7d), "month" (30d), "year" (365d).
        
        Default is None.

topic.description:
Specifies search category for optimized results.
   
        Use "general" (default) for most queries, INCLUDING those with terms like 
        "latest," "newest," or "recent" when referring to general information.

        Use "finance" for markets, investments, economic data, or financial news.

        Use "news" ONLY for politics, sports, or major current events covered by 
        mainstream media - NOT simply because a query asks for "new" information.
